items.title: Introduction: major, minor and trace components

source_refs.note: Unnumbered introduction, printed page 305. The learning outcomes are not reproduced.

blocks.text: The atmosphere is a sphere of different gases around the earth. Its components may be divided into major, minor and trace components. The major components are nitrogen (78.00 per cent) and oxygen (21.01 per cent); the minor components are argon (0.93 per cent) and carbon dioxide (0.04 per cent); the trace components are methane, hydrogen, neon, helium, krypton and xenon.

blocks.caption: Composition of the atmosphere
rows: methane, hydrogen, neon, helium, krypton, xenon

blocks.prompt: Carbon dioxide is only a minor component of the air. Why does it matter so much for climate?
blocks.explanation: Although it is only about 0.04 per cent of the atmosphere, carbon dioxide absorbs the long-wave heat radiated by the earth, so even small increases in its concentration trap more heat (the greenhouse effect, 14.7); nitrogen and oxygen, the major gases, do not absorb infrared in this way.

items: Atmosphere: N2 78.00% and O2 21.01% (major); Ar 0.93% and CO2 0.04% (minor); CH4, H2, Ne, He, Kr, Xe (trace).
